publication: Source chart committed to main; no helm-v0.4.0 archive has been published.
render_check_names: single SQLite writer, retained PVC, pinned image and separate probes
Kubernetes 1.33 baseline accepts OpenShift 4.20 and retains 1.34/1.37 Kubernetes defaults
opt-in HTTPS edge Route targets the private named Service port and uses the router certificate
Route can disable insecure HTTP instead of redirecting it
restricted-v2 profile delegates identities and SELinux, hardens Deployment and Helm hook without SCC grants
OpenShift example starts privately with no Route and needs no Route API for bootstrap
existing PVC is referenced without taking ownership
PostgreSQL uses existing database/key Secrets and independent scratch space
OpenShift Route and restricted-v2 profile compose with shared PostgreSQL replicas
OpenShift network example scopes router, health hook and workload collectors without changing model/egress policy
restricted-v2 recovery example uses the same pinned image and delegates volume identity without starting a server
multi-DC, HTTPS ingress, HPA, PDB and network policy render together
release-scoped topology spread, controlled Secret revision and unhealthy pod eviction
optional monitoring uses a scoped Secret reference and workspace-deduplicated alerts

The OpenShift profile is exercised with synthetic admission-assigned identities, not real SCC admission or a router. No Prometheus Operator reconciliation, zone failure, incompatible schema downgrade or model capacity certification.

boundaries: Real published 2.5.0 image and its pinned 2.4.1 predecessor, synthetic HTTP model Services and disposable single-node kind clusters.
OpenShift Route resources server-validated using an official checksum-pinned schema installed only in the disposable tests.
Arbitrary UID/fsGroup runtime checks use explicit synthetic identities under Kubernetes Restricted Pod Security Admission, not actual SCC admission.

No real OpenShift cluster was available. CRI-O/SELinux, CSI permissions, Route admission/TLS/SSE, OVN policies, monitoring operator/alert delivery and organization IdP require documented target-cluster acceptance.
The user selected completion with automated tests and the installation guide; no OpenShift certification or production availability claim.
